_comment: Stock scene-construction phrases that parallel authoring agents independently reach for, which BP13 (bookPatternAudit) flags when the same verbatim 5-token run appears across >= max(3, ceil(N*0.1)) chapters. This list is INJECTED into each STEP-2 agent (see STEP-2-WRITE-CHAPTERS.md) as phrases to avoid AND as a pattern of what to vary. It is NOT a deterministic gate input — BP13 is data-driven and finds repeats emergently; this list is preventive guidance. Add offenders here as new books surface them. 2026-06-10 catalog campaign: house TIC PHRASES added ("the point is" appeared 240x across all 26 books, "the question is" 107x, "scoreboard" 42x) — these are shorter than the 5-token BP13 window, so they are PREVENTIVE guidance for authors, with budgets enforced at refresh time via catalog-audit.
principle: Never let a 5-word run repeat across chapters. Vary the GRAMMAR of how a scene opens, how a decision is framed, and how a consequence lands — not just the nouns. If two of your scenarios could swap their opening clause without anyone noticing, rewrite one.
openerPatternsToVary: Name + present-tense verb + at + place (e.g. 'Marit stares at the dashboard')
Time-of-day anchor opener (e.g. 'By Thursday, the team...')
Consequence-first opener (state the result, then the cause)
